hints.title: Bivariate Rejection Sampling Transformation
hints.text: Generating a uniform distribution over a larger discrete target set requires composing smaller uniform random calls and rejecting out-of-range outcomes.

hints.title: Two-Dimensional Discrete Coordinate Mapping
hints.text: Combining two 7-sided rolls yields forty-nine uniformly distributed indices. Truncating the sample space to forty produces a multiple of ten with equal likelihood.

hints.title: Rejection Sampling Blueprint
hints.text: Loop indefinitely: row = rand7(), col = rand7(), idx = (row - 1) * 7 + col. If idx <= 40, return 1 + (idx - 1) % 10. Otherwise reject and continue sampling.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: Calls: expected 2.45 calls to rand7 per rand10
complexity.notes: Acceptance probability per round is 40 / 49 (~81.6%), leading to expected constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple modular arithmetic on the sum of two rolls does not yield uniform probabilities.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant space rejection sampling preserves strict mathematical uniformity.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding why (rand7() - 1) * 7 + rand7() creates a flat 1..49 distribution.
